name: What is the difference between a bid, budget, and estimate?

mainEntity.name: How are a construction budget, estimate, and bid different in practice?
mainEntity.text: How are a construction budget, estimate, and bid different in practice?

acceptedAnswer.text: A construction budget, estimate, and bid are related but not the same thing. A budget is the owner’s early planning target, usually based on a rough idea of scope and finish level. An estimate is a more refined cost forecast prepared from drawings, quantities, and assumptions. A bid is a contractor’s pricing offer for a defined scope of work, often used for selection and contract formation. In Los Angeles residential projects, confusion between these terms creates a lot of budget problems. A homeowner may think they have a final number when they really only have a planning budget. The most dependable process is to start with a budget, move to a conceptual estimate, and then request a bid after the scope is clear. That sequence gives the best chance of keeping the project on track financially.
acceptedAnswer.description: A budget is an early planning number, an estimate is a more detailed cost prediction, and a bid is a contractor’s price to do defined work. Budgets are flexible, estimates are informational, and bids become more binding once the scope is clearly set.
